title: Maruti Suzuki faces vehicle shortage ahead of festive season, supplies to improve from January 2027- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: Maruti Suzuki's domestic passenger vehicle market share rose 2.38 percentage points during April-July FY27, but production has lagged demand.   September 11, 2026 / 12:57 IST             Maruti Suzuki India is heading into the festive season with strong sales and market share growth, but production constraints have left the country's largest carmaker with around 1.80 lakh pending bookings and only 15-16 days of stock. "We will have good supplies from January 2027 onwards," Partho Banerjee, Senior Executive Officer, Marketing and Sales, Maruti Suzuki India, told Moneycontrol. "We have 1.80 lakh pending bookings. We have network stock for only 15-16 days. Had we got 30 days of network stock, then in the festive time, we would have fired on all cylinders. We are short of vehicles for the festive season," he said. Last year, during the festive period from September 22 to October 31, Maruti Suzuki received more than 5,00,000 bookings and sold over 4,10,000 vehicles. Banerjee observed that the company's two new production plants need time to reach their rated capacity as they are highly automated. Maruti Suzuki's domestic passenger vehicle (PV) wholesales increased 35.77 per cent year-on-year to 7,21,431 units during April-July FY27 from 5,31,348 units in the year-ago period, while the industry grew 28.02 per cent to 17,31,621 units from 13,52,656 units. Consequently, the company's domestic PV market share rose to 41.66 per cent from 39.28 per cent, an increase of 2.38 percentage points, based on data from the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM). This marked a recovery after the decline in FY26, when the carmaker's market share fell to 39.26 per cent from 40.93 per cent in FY25. Maruti Suzuki's domestic wholesales rose 3.5 per cent to 18,23,129 units in FY26, while the industry grew 7.9 per cent to 46,43,439 units. Banerjee said Maruti Suzuki aims to grow faster than the industry in FY27, although the outcome will depend on how quickly production can be increased. "In the 18 per cent GST bracket, the industry is growing by 30 per cent, and we are growing by 36 per cent. In the 40 per cent GST bracket, the industry is growing by 22 per cent, and we are growing by 30 per cent. Overall, the industry is growing by 28 per cent, and we are growing by around 36 per cent," Banerjee noted. Maruti Suzuki's annual installed production capacity has reached 29,00,000 units following the commissioning of the fourth plant at its Hansalpur complex in Gujarat and the second plant at Kharkhoda in Haryana this year. Hansalpur accounts for 10,00,000 units of capacity, followed by Manesar at 9,00,000 units. Kharkhoda and Gurugram can produce 5,00,000 units each annually. The carmaker has raised its planned FY27 capital expenditure by 40 per cent to Rs 14,000 crore. The Brezza SUV-maker is targeting an investment of Rs 77,500 crore through FY31 as it works towards reaching an annual capacity of 40,00,000 units. Banerjee linked the revival in small car demand to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) restructuring implemented on September 22, 2025, which improved affordability. Under GST 2.0, sub-4 metre cars with petrol engines below 1,200 cc or diesel engines below 1,500 cc attract a flat 18 per cent GST. Larger internal combustion engine (ICE) cars are taxed at 40 per cent. There is no compensation cess now. He said the changes offset part of the price increases caused by regulatory additions. Among Maruti Suzuki's small cars, the WagonR sales stood at 77,014 units during April-July 2026, while the Alto K10 recorded 43,665 units. Maruti Suzuki began domestic sales of the e Vitara in February 2026 after exports started in August 2025, but production capacity has limited volumes. Asked what was holding back its domestic sales, Banerjee said, "Production capacity. That is it." "There are commitments for exports. There is a capacity which has been allocated for the domestic market. We are playing as per the game. The day we are allotted more, we will ramp up," he added. Maruti Suzuki India is Suzuki Motor Corporation's exclusive global production hub for the e Vitara. The electric SUV was earlier manufactured at Hansalpur on a line shared with the Fronx compact SUV, limiting output, but will now be produced exclusively at the newly commissioned fourth plant there. The carmaker exported 15,210 units of the e Vitara during April-June FY27, accounting for about 97 per cent of India's electric car shipments. However, its domestic sales stood at around 5,000 units during the same quarter. Banerjee said the company needed another three to four months to raise e Vitara production to the desired level.
